recommended_treatment.Low: Topical salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide daily.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Topical retinoids (e.g., adapalene 0.1%) combined with topical clindamycin.
recommended_treatment.High: Oral doxycycline (100mg twice daily) combined with topical benzoyl peroxide.

Acne.medication_category: Topical Keratolytics, Topical Retinoids, Tetracycline Antibiotics
Acne.lifestyle_recommendations: Wash face twice daily with a gentle cleanser, avoid picking lesions, use non-comedogenic skincare products.
Acne.contraindications: Avoid oral doxycycline during pregnancy or in children under 8 years of age.
Acne.red_flags: Severe facial swelling, high fever, or signs of secondary skin infection.
Acne.emergency_referral_conditions: Signs of facial cellulitis or systemic sepsis.
Acne.follow_up: Re-evaluate clinical response in 6 to 8 weeks.
Acne.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Acne.rationale: Topical keratolytics act first-line for mild acne by promoting desquamation. Severe cases require tetracyclines to address deep follicular inflammation.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Acetaminophen (500mg every 6 hours as needed) and topical NSAID gel (diclofenac 1%).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Ibuprofen (400mg three times daily) with proton pump inhibitor gastroprotection.
recommended_treatment.High: Oral Prednisone short-course or initiation of DMARD (e.g., Methotrexate) under rheumatology direction.

Arthritis.lifestyle_recommendations: Gentle low-impact exercise (swimming, cycling), weight management, joint protection techniques.
Arthritis.contraindications: NSAIDs are contraindicated in active peptic ulcer disease, severe renal impairment, or severe heart failure.
Arthritis.red_flags: Single joint that is hot, red, swollen, and exquisitely painful with systemic fever.
Arthritis.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected septic arthritis or acute joint dislocation.
Arthritis.follow_up: Review pain management and joint function in 4 weeks.
Arthritis.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Arthritis.rationale: Pain relief starts with paracetamol and topical agents to minimize systemic NSAID side effects. Autoimmune flare-ups require steroid intervention.

recommended_treatment.Low: As-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (e.g., budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Regular daily low-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol.
recommended_treatment.High: Medium-to-high dose maintenance ICS-formoterol; refer for oral corticosteroid trial.

Bronchial Asthma.lifestyle_recommendations: Identify and avoid triggers (dust mites, pet dander, tobacco smoke). Monitor peak flow.
Bronchial Asthma.contraindications: Do not use long-acting beta-agonists without inhaled corticosteroids (black box warning).
Bronchial Asthma.red_flags: Use of rescue inhaler > 3 times per week, waking up at night with asthma symptoms.
Bronchial Asthma.emergency_referral_conditions: Silent chest, cyanosis (blue lips/face), inability to speak full sentences, peak flow < 50% personal best.
Bronchial Asthma.follow_up: Check inhaler technique and review asthma control in 2 to 4 weeks.
Bronchial Asthma.rationale: ICS-formoterol provides rapid bronchodilation while simultaneously treating the underlying airway inflammation to prevent exacerbations.

recommended_treatment.Low: Physical therapy assessment, active neck stretching, and Acetaminophen for pain.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Naproxen (500mg twice daily) and a short course of muscle relaxant (Cyclobenzaprine 5mg at night).
recommended_treatment.High: Gabapentin (100mg three times daily) for radiculopathy, and evaluation for surgical decompression.

Cervical spondylosis.lifestyle_recommendations: Practice good posture, adjust computer screens to eye level, perform isometric neck strengthening.
Cervical spondylosis.contraindications: Avoid cervical manipulation/chiropractic cracking in patients with radicular symptoms.
Cervical spondylosis.red_flags: Progressive muscle weakness in hands or arms, gait instability, bowel/bladder incontinence.
Cervical spondylosis.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute spinal cord compression symptoms (cervical myelopathy).
Cervical spondylosis.rationale: Conservative management with physical therapy and NSAIDs resolve most mechanical cases. Radiculopathy requires gabapentinoids.

recommended_treatment.Low: Supportive care: Calamine lotion, cool baths, oral Paracetamol for fever.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Acyclovir (800mg 5 times daily for 5 days) if started within 24 hours of rash onset in high-risk patients.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous Acyclovir (10mg/kg every 8 hours) for severe/complicated cases.

Chicken pox.lifestyle_recommendations: Keep fingernails short to prevent scratching and secondary infection, wear loose clothing, isolate.
Chicken pox.contraindications: Aspirin is strictly contraindicated due to the risk of Reye's Syndrome in viral infections.
Chicken pox.red_flags: Extreme drowsiness, confusion, shortness of breath, or bleeding into the chickenpox spots.
Chicken pox.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected varicella pneumonia, encephalitis, or severe secondary skin sepsis.
Chicken pox.follow_up: Monitor closely for 7 to 10 days until all lesions have crusted over.
Chicken pox.evidence_source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
Chicken pox.rationale: Symptomatic care is sufficient for healthy children. Antivirals are indicated for older patients or severe complications to suppress replication.

recommended_treatment.Low: Hydration, rest, saline nasal sprays, and steam inhalation.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Pseudoephedrine (60mg every 6 hours) for congestion, Acetaminophen for sore throat.
recommended_treatment.High: Evaluation for secondary bacterial sinusitis or bronchitis if symptoms worsen past 10 days.

Common Cold.lifestyle_recommendations: Drink warm liquids, wash hands frequently, gargle with salt water, get adequate sleep.
Common Cold.contraindications: Do not give OTC cough and cold medicines to children under 6 years. Avoid pseudoephedrine in severe hypertension.
Common Cold.red_flags: Difficulty breathing, persistent high fever (>38.5C) lasting more than 3 days.
Common Cold.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute respiratory distress or severe chest pain.
Common Cold.follow_up: Self-monitor. Review if symptoms do not improve within 10 to 14 days.
Common Cold.rationale: Colds are self-limiting viral infections. Antibiotics are contraindicated and have no effect. Management focuses on symptomatic relief.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral hydration (WHO Oral Rehydration Salts), strict rest, Paracetamol (500mg) for fever.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Close monitoring of complete blood counts (hematocrit/platelets) every 12 to 24 hours. Intravenous crystalloids if oral intake is poor.
recommended_treatment.High: Emergency hospitalization for IV fluid management and platelet transfusion.

Dengue.lifestyle_recommendations: Rest in bed, stay hydrated with electrolyte solutions, use mosquito netting and insect repellents.
Dengue.contraindications: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin, naproxen) are contraindicated due to bleeding risk from platelet dysfunction.
Dengue.red_flags: Persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding gums or nose, cold clammy extremities, lethargy.
Dengue.emergency_referral_conditions: Severe dengue shock syndrome (DSS) or dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
Dengue.follow_up: Daily monitoring of platelet count until fever subsides for 48 hours.
Dengue.rationale: Dengue treatment is supportive. Fluid management is critical to offset plasma leakage. NSAIDs are avoided to prevent fatal hemorrhage.

recommended_treatment.Low: High-fiber diet (25-30g daily), fiber supplements (Psyllium), and warm sitz baths.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Topical hydrocortisone cream (1% for max 7 days) and oral stool softeners (Docusate).
recommended_treatment.High: Surgical evaluation for rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, or hemorrhoidectomy.

Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.medication_category: Topical Corticosteroids, Stool Softeners, Fiber Laxatives
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.lifestyle_recommendations: Increase water intake, avoid straining during defecation, avoid sitting on toilet for >5 minutes.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.contraindications: Do not use topical steroids for more than 7 days to prevent skin atrophy.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.red_flags: Large volume rectal bleeding, severe persistent rectal pain, fever.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.emergency_referral_conditions: Strangulated, thrombosed hemorrhoid causing excruciating pain.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.rationale: Initial management is dietary to reduce stool hardness. Short-course topical steroids address acute inflammation.

recommended_treatment.Low: Topical Clotrimazole (1%) or Miconazole cream twice daily for 2 weeks.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Topical Terbinafine (1%) cream daily for 1 week; add oral Fluconazole (150mg single dose) if widespread.
recommended_treatment.High: Oral Terbinafine (250mg daily) for 2 to 4 weeks (requires baseline liver function tests).

Fungal infection.lifestyle_recommendations: Keep affected skin clean and dry, wear loose cotton clothing, avoid sharing towels/linens.
Fungal infection.contraindications: Oral terbinafine is contraindicated in active or chronic liver disease.
Fungal infection.red_flags: Spreading redness, warmth, pus, or fever (indicating secondary bacterial infection).
Fungal infection.emergency_referral_conditions: Severe systemic symptoms in immunocompromised patients.
Fungal infection.follow_up: Review in 2 weeks if no improvement.
Fungal infection.rationale: Topical azoles/allylamines effectively clear localized dermatophyte infections. Widespread cases require systemic oral therapy.

recommended_treatment.Low: Dietary modification (DASH diet) and sodium restriction (<2g daily); review in 3 months.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Initiate single-agent therapy (e.g., Lisinopril 10mg daily or Amlodipine 5mg daily).
recommended_treatment.High: Dual-agent therapy (e.g., Lisinopril 20mg + Amlodipine 5mg daily) and close monitoring.

Hypertension.medication_category: ACE Inhibitors, Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs), Calcium Channel Blockers (CCBs)
Hypertension.lifestyle_recommendations: Adopt DASH diet, perform 150 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly, limit alcohol, quit smoking.
Hypertension.contraindications: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal renal toxicity.
Hypertension.red_flags: Blood pressure reading > 180/120 mmHg, chest pain, vision changes, severe headache.
Hypertension.emergency_referral_conditions: Hypertensive emergency (BP > 180/120 mmHg with acute target organ damage).
Hypertension.follow_up: Re-check blood pressure in 2 weeks after initiating or altering medication.
Hypertension.rationale: Pharmacotherapy choice is tailored by risk profile. ACEi/CCB serve as first-line agents to reduce cardiovascular stroke risk.

recommended_treatment.Low: Topical Hydrogen Peroxide (1%) cream or topical Mupirocin (2%) ointment 3 times daily for 5 days.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Cephalexin (500mg 4 times daily) or Flucloxacillin for 5 to 7 days.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous antibiotics for extensive, bullous impetigo with systemic symptoms.

Impetigo.lifestyle_recommendations: Gently wash honey-colored crusts with soap and water, wash hands frequently, isolate towels.
Impetigo.contraindications: Avoid topical mupirocin overuse to prevent resistance in MRSA strains.
Impetigo.red_flags: Rapid spread of lesions near the eyes, high fever, or severe lethargy.
Impetigo.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome or cellulitis.
Impetigo.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Impetigo.rationale: Localized impetigo is treated topically to minimize systemic antibiotic side effects. Widespread lesions require oral antibiotics.

recommended_treatment.Low: Investigatory workup: liver function tests, abdominal ultrasound, and supportive hydration.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Identify and treat specific cause (e.g. stop suspected drug, treat hepatitis).
recommended_treatment.High: Hospitalization for biliary decompression or liver support therapy.

Jaundice.medication_category: Supportive Agents, Anti-pruritics (Cholestyramine) if biliary obstruction
Jaundice.lifestyle_recommendations: Eat a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet, maintain hydration, avoid all hepatotoxins.
Jaundice.contraindications: Strictly avoid alcohol, acetaminophen (paracetamol), and other hepatotoxic medications.
Jaundice.red_flags: Confusion, flapping hand tremor (asterixis), bleeding tendency, severe abdominal distension.
Jaundice.follow_up: Repeat liver function panels every 48 to 72 hours until stable.
Jaundice.evidence_source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
Jaundice.rationale: Jaundice is a symptom of underlying liver dysfunction. Rest and removal of hepatotoxic agents protect parenchymal cells.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Artemether-lumefantrine (ACT) or Chloroquine depending on local resistance patterns.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral ACT with close clinical monitoring; add Primaquine for P. vivax relapse prevention.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous Artesunate (2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, and 24 hours, then daily).

Malaria.medication_category: Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT), Primaquine, IV Artesunate
Malaria.lifestyle_recommendations: Stay hydrated, rest in bed, wear long-sleeved clothing, sleep under insecticidal nets.
Malaria.contraindications: Primaquine is contraindicated in patients with G6PD deficiency due to risk of severe hemolysis.
Malaria.red_flags: Altered consciousness, severe anemia, persistent vomiting, dark urine.
Malaria.emergency_referral_conditions: Severe malaria (cerebral malaria, severe anemia, pulmonary edema).
Malaria.follow_up: Verify parasite clearance with blood smears at 48 hours and 7 days.
Malaria.rationale: ACT is first-line for uncomplicated malaria to clear blood-stage parasites. Severe malaria requires rapid IV artesunate.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Ibuprofen (400mg) or Acetaminophen (500mg) combined with oral Caffeine.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Sumatriptan (500mg) at onset of headache, combined with an antiemetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous hydration, Ketorolac (30mg IV), and initiation of prophylactic beta-blockers (Propranolol).

Migraine.lifestyle_recommendations: Keep a headache diary, maintain a consistent sleep schedule, stay hydrated, avoid skipped meals.
Migraine.contraindications: Triptans are contraindicated in patients with ischemic heart disease, coronary vasospasm, or uncontrolled hypertension.
Migraine.red_flags: Sudden onset 'thunderclap' headache, headache with neck stiffness, fever, or focal neurological signs.
Migraine.follow_up: Review headache diary and abortive therapy response in 4 weeks.
Migraine.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Migraine.rationale: First-line therapies target peripheral inflammation. Triptans are selective 5-HT agonists used to reverse cerebral vasodilation.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Amoxicillin (500mg three times daily) or Doxycycline for 5 days.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Levofloxacin (500mg daily) or combination of Amoxicillin + Azithromycin for 5 to 7 days.
recommended_treatment.High: Hospitalization for IV Ceftriaxone + Azithromycin, oxygen supplementation, and monitoring.

Pneumonia.lifestyle_recommendations: Get complete rest, stay hydrated, avoid smoking, perform deep breathing exercises.
Pneumonia.contraindications: Fluoroquinolones are contraindicated in patients with a history of tendonitis or aortic aneurysm.
Pneumonia.red_flags: Respiratory rate > 30/min, oxygen saturation < 92% on room air, confusion.
Pneumonia.emergency_referral_conditions: Severe respiratory failure, septic shock, or CURB-65 score >= 3.
Pneumonia.follow_up: Check clinical recovery in 48 hours; repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks.
Pneumonia.evidence_source: American Thoracic Society (ATS) / Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA)
Pneumonia.rationale: Antibiotics target common atypical and typical pathogens. Empiric scaling depends on patient comorbidities and severity score.

recommended_treatment.Low: Topical emollients (ointments) and mild topical Corticosteroids (e.g. Hydrocortisone 1%).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Potent topical Corticosteroids (e.g. Betamethasone) combined with Calcipotriene (Vitamin D analogue).
recommended_treatment.High: Refer for Phototherapy (UVB) or systemic therapy (Methotrexate or Biologics like Adalimumab).

Psoriasis.medication_category: Topical Emollients, Topical Corticosteroids, Vitamin D Analogues, Systemic Immunosuppressants
Psoriasis.lifestyle_recommendations: Keep skin moist, take lukewarm baths, avoid scratching lesions, practice stress reduction.
Psoriasis.contraindications: Avoid sudden withdrawal of potent systemic steroids, which can trigger erythrodermic flares.
Psoriasis.red_flags: Widespread painful skin redness with sheets of pustules and systemic fever.
Psoriasis.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected generalized pustular psoriasis or erythrodermic psoriasis.
Psoriasis.follow_up: Evaluate topical treatment response in 4 weeks.
Psoriasis.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Psoriasis.rationale: Topical steroids suppress immune hyperactivation in the dermis. High-severity cases require systemic immunosuppressants.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Azithromycin (500mg daily) for 7 days with strict home isolation.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Ciprofloxacin (500mg twice daily) or Azithromycin for 10-14 days with daily blood checks.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous Ceftriaxone (2g daily) for 10 to 14 days and close monitoring.

Typhoid.lifestyle_recommendations: Drink boiled or bottled water only, eat fully cooked hot foods, wash hands thoroughly.
Typhoid.contraindications: Avoid fluoroquinolones in regions with known high quinolone resistance profiles.
Typhoid.red_flags: Severe abdominal pain, bloody stools, persistent vomiting, altered consciousness.
Typhoid.follow_up: Three stool cultures must be negative at 1 week post-treatment before clearing.
Typhoid.rationale: Antibiotic therapy eradicates Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. Quinolone resistance requires scaling to azithromycin.

recommended_treatment.Low: Leg elevation, regular walking, and weight loss support.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Graduated compression stockings (Class II, 20-30 mmHg) worn during the day.
recommended_treatment.High: Vascular surgical referral for endothermal ablation or sclerotherapy.

Varicose Veins.lifestyle_recommendations: Avoid prolonged standing or sitting, elevate legs above heart level, exercise calf muscles.
Varicose Veins.contraindications: Compression stockings are contraindicated in severe peripheral arterial disease (ABPI < 0.8).
Varicose Veins.red_flags: Sudden painful swelling in a single leg, warm skin, or ulceration near the ankle.
Varicose Veins.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or active bleeding from a ruptured varicose vein.
Varicose Veins.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
Varicose Veins.rationale: Lifestyle changes and compression garments improve venous return. Severe anatomical reflux requires vein ablation.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Cetirizine (10mg daily) or Loratadine as needed for mild symptoms.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Fluticasone propionate nasal spray (2 sprays per nostril daily) + oral antihistamine.
recommended_treatment.High: Intramuscular Epinephrine (0.3mg, e.g. EpiPen) immediately, followed by emergency room visit.

allergy.medication_category: Second-generation H1 Antihistamines, Nasal Corticosteroids, Epinephrine
allergy.lifestyle_recommendations: Avoid known allergen triggers, use HEPA air filters, rinse sinuses with saline.
allergy.contraindications: Avoid sedating first-generation antihistamines in elderly patients due to fall and anticholinergic risks.
allergy.red_flags: Swelling of lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty swallowing, wheezing, dizziness.
allergy.emergency_referral_conditions: Anaphylaxis (multi-system allergic reaction with respiratory or cardiovascular involvement).
allergy.follow_up: Check back in 2 weeks to evaluate drug efficacy.
allergy.evidence_source: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
allergy.rationale: Second-generation antihistamines block peripheral H1 receptors. Anaphylaxis requires intramuscular epinephrine.

recommended_treatment.Low: Dietary modification, weight loss program, and Metformin (500mg daily) titration.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Metformin (1000mg twice daily) combined with a GLP-1 receptor agonist (e.g. Semaglutide).
recommended_treatment.High: Initiate Basal Insulin (e.g., Glargine 10 units daily) and refer to Endocrinology.

diabetes.medication_category: Biguanides (Metformin), GLP-1 Receptor Agonists, Basal/Bolus Insulins
diabetes.lifestyle_recommendations: Maintain low-carbohydrate diet, perform 150 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly, conduct daily foot self-inspections.
diabetes.contraindications: Metformin is contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2) due to lactic acidosis risk.
diabetes.red_flags: Blood glucose > 250 mg/dL with ketones in urine, confusion, rapid deep breathing, extreme thirst.
diabetes.emergency_referral_conditions: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) or Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS).
diabetes.follow_up: Check HbA1c level every 3 months until target (<7%) is achieved, then every 6 months.
diabetes.rationale: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose output. Escalating to insulin is required when oral agents fail to control hyperglycemia.

recommended_treatment.Low: Stop the offending drug immediately. Apply Hydrocortisone (1%) topical cream for pruritus.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Stop drug; initiate oral Prednisone (40mg daily tapered over 5 days) + oral antihistamine.
recommended_treatment.High: Admit to hospital, administer IV fluids, IV Methylprednisolone, and manage skin care.

drug reaction.lifestyle_recommendations: Clearly document the drug name and reaction type, inform all pharmacies, wear an alert bracelet.
drug reaction.contraindications: Do not re-expose the patient to the offending drug or cross-reactive medication classes.
drug reaction.red_flags: Skin peeling, blistering, mucous membrane lesions (mouth, eyes, genitals), high fever.
drug reaction.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), or DRESS syndrome.
drug reaction.follow_up: Verify complete resolution of skin symptoms in 1 week.
drug reaction.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
drug reaction.rationale: Immediate withdrawal of the offending antigen is the single most critical intervention. Steroids mitigate hypersensitivity.

recommended_treatment.Low: Lifestyle and dietary changes; take antacids (calcium carbonate) as needed.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Take Famotidine (20mg twice daily) or Omeprazole (20mg daily) for a 4-to-8 week course.
recommended_treatment.High: Increase Omeprazole to 40mg daily and evaluate for anti-reflux surgery (Nissen fundoplication).

gastroesophageal reflux disease.medication_category: Antacids, H2 Receptor Antagonists (H2RAs), Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs)
gastroesophageal reflux disease.lifestyle_recommendations: Eat smaller meals, avoid lying down for 3 hours after eating, elevate the head of the bed, lose weight.
gastroesophageal reflux disease.contraindications: Long-term PPI use should be avoided without periodic review due to fracture and B12 deficiency risks.
gastroesophageal reflux disease.red_flags: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia), painful swallowing (odynophagia), vomiting blood, iron-deficiency anemia.
gastroesophageal reflux disease.emergency_referral_conditions: Severe chest pain radiating to back or arm (rule out acute coronary syndrome).
gastroesophageal reflux disease.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
gastroesophageal reflux disease.rationale: PPIs covalently bind and inhibit the H+/K+ ATPase pump in gastric parietal cells, significantly raising stomach pH.

recommended_treatment.Low: Omeprazole (20mg daily) for 4 weeks. Stop NSAID use.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Perform H. pylori testing; if positive, initiate triple therapy: Omeprazole + Amoxicillin + Clarithromycin.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous Pantoprazole infusion, complete bowel rest, and urgent upper endoscopy.

peptic ulcer disease.lifestyle_recommendations: Avoid all NSAID drugs, stop smoking, limit alcohol, avoid late-night snacks.
peptic ulcer disease.contraindications: Do not administer clarithromycin in patients taking simvastatin due to severe myopathy risk.
peptic ulcer disease.red_flags: Sudden severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood, black tarry stools (melena).
peptic ulcer disease.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute gastrointestinal bleeding or gastrointestinal perforation.
peptic ulcer disease.follow_up: Confirm H. pylori eradication using a urea breath test 4 weeks after finishing antibiotics.
peptic ulcer disease.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
peptic ulcer disease.rationale: Acid suppression promotes mucosal healing. Eradicating H. pylori is necessary to prevent recurrent ulceration.

recommended_treatment.Low: Oral Nitrofurantoin (100mg modified-release twice daily) for 3 days (females) or 7 days (males).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (160/800mg twice daily) for 3 days; obtain urine culture.
recommended_treatment.High: Intravenous Ceftriaxone (1g daily) or Piperacillin-tazobactam for pyelonephritis.

urinary tract infection.medication_category: First-line Urinary Antibacterials, Sulfonamides, IV Cephalosporins
urinary tract infection.lifestyle_recommendations: Increase water intake, urinate after intercourse, wipe from front to back.
urinary tract infection.contraindications: Nitrofurantoin is ineffective and contraindicated in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min.
urinary tract infection.red_flags: High fever, chills, severe flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting.
urinary tract infection.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected urosepsis or acute pyelonephritis with hemodynamic instability.
urinary tract infection.follow_up: Self-monitor. Review if symptoms do not fully resolve within 48 hours of starting antibiotics.
urinary tract infection.evidence_source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
urinary tract infection.rationale: Nitrofurantoin concentrates highly in the bladder urine. Pyelonephritis requires systemic IV cephalosporins.

recommended_treatment.Low: Sublingual Nitroglycerin (0.4mg as needed for acute chest discomfort), low-dose Aspirin (81mg daily), and lifestyle risk modification.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Oral Beta-Blocker (Metoprolol succinate 50mg daily) plus high-intensity Statin (Atorvastatin 80mg daily) and sublingual Nitroglycerin.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent cardiology referral for diagnostic coronary angiography; Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (Aspirin + Clopidogrel) and IV Nitroglycerin.

angina.medication_category: Organic Nitrates, Beta-Blockers, Antiplatelets, HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors
angina.lifestyle_recommendations: Adopt Mediterranean diet, engage in supervised cardiac rehabilitation, avoid heavy isometric exertion, achieve smoking cessation.
angina.contraindications: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (e.g. Sildenafil) are strictly contraindicated with Nitrates due to severe refractory hypotension.
angina.red_flags: Chest pain lasting > 20 minutes, pain unrelieved by 3 doses of sublingual nitroglycerin, diaphoresis, syncope, hypotension.
angina.emergency_referral_conditions: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (unstable angina or myocardial infarction), hemodynamic instability.
angina.follow_up: Cardiology clinic follow-up within 1 to 2 weeks for stress testing.
angina.evidence_source: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC)
angina.rationale: Nitrates provide rapid coronary vasodilation while beta-blockers reduce myocardial oxygen demand. High-risk presentations require invasive evaluation.

recommended_treatment.Low: Electrolyte optimization (potassium > 4.0 mEq/L, magnesium > 2.0 mg/dL), caffeine and alcohol reduction, 24-48h Holter monitoring.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Rate control with Metoprolol succinate (25-50mg daily) or Diltiazem; 12-lead ECG and echocardiography.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent electrical or pharmacological cardioversion under continuous cardiac telemetry; antiarrhythmic therapy (Amiodarone).

arrhythmia.medication_category: Antiarrhythmics (Class I-IV), Beta-Blockers, Calcium Channel Blockers
arrhythmia.lifestyle_recommendations: Avoid stimulants (caffeine, energy drinks, nicotine), manage stress, maintain adequate hydration and sleep.
arrhythmia.contraindications: Class IC antiarrhythmics (Flecainide) are contraindicated in patients with structural heart disease or prior myocardial infarction.
arrhythmia.red_flags: Sustained ventricular tachycardia, syncope, chest pain with palpitations, systolic BP < 90 mmHg.
arrhythmia.emergency_referral_conditions: Hemodynamically unstable tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, wide-complex tachycardia.
arrhythmia.follow_up: Electrophysiology review with Holter monitoring results within 2 to 4 weeks.
arrhythmia.guideline_version: HRS/ACC/AHA Ventricular and Supraventricular Arrhythmia Guidelines 2024
arrhythmia.rationale: Asymptomatic ectopic beats require conservative trigger management. Hemodynamically compromising arrhythmias necessitate rapid stabilization.

recommended_treatment.Low: CHA2DS2-VASc stroke risk assessment; rate control with Metoprolol or Diltiazem if symptomatic.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC: Apixaban 5mg twice daily or Rivaroxaban 20mg daily) if CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2; rate control.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent rate control with IV Diltiazem/Metoprolol or synchronized electrical cardioversion if unstable; therapeutic anticoagulation.

atrial fibrillation.medication_category: DOACs (Factor Xa Inhibitors), Beta-Blockers, Non-Dihydropyridine CCBs, Antiarrhythmics
atrial fibrillation.lifestyle_recommendations: Strict limitation of alcohol intake (holiday heart avoidance), weight loss, screening for obstructive sleep apnea.
atrial fibrillation.contraindications: DOACs are contraindicated in mechanical heart valves or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis (use Warfarin).
atrial fibrillation.red_flags: Rapid ventricular response (HR > 150 bpm) with hypotension, acute shortness of breath, sudden focal neurological deficit.
atrial fibrillation.emergency_referral_conditions: Hemodynamically unstable AFib with angina or pulmonary edema; acute ischemic stroke symptoms.
atrial fibrillation.follow_up: Cardiology clinic follow-up within 4 weeks to assess anticoagulation adherence and rhythm control.
atrial fibrillation.evidence_source: American College of Cardiology (ACC) / AHA / HRS
atrial fibrillation.rationale: Anticoagulation is the primary therapeutic priority to prevent thromboembolic stroke. Rate vs rhythm control is selected based on symptoms.

recommended_treatment.Low: Aspirin (81mg daily), high-intensity Statin (Atorvastatin 40-80mg), strict BP control (<130/80 mmHg), and lifestyle modification.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Add Beta-Blocker (Carvedilol or Metoprolol) and ACE-inhibitor (Lisinopril 10-20mg); non-invasive myocardial perfusion imaging.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or CABG; Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (Aspirin + Ticagrelor/Clopidogrel).

coronary artery disease.medication_category: Antiplatelets, Statins, ACE Inhibitors / ARBs, Beta-Blockers
coronary artery disease.lifestyle_recommendations: Heart-healthy diet (low saturated fats, high fiber), 150 mins/week moderate aerobic exercise, complete tobacco cessation.
coronary artery disease.contraindications: NSAIDs (except aspirin) should be avoided due to increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk.
coronary artery disease.red_flags: Accelerating frequency or duration of chest pain, pain at rest, dynamic ST-T wave ECG changes.
coronary artery disease.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest.
coronary artery disease.follow_up: Outpatient cardiology assessment and lipid panel review in 4 to 6 weeks.
coronary artery disease.guideline_version: AHA/ACC Coronary Artery Disease Management Standards 2024
coronary artery disease.rationale: Plaque stabilization through aggressive statin therapy and antiplatelet inhibition prevents acute thrombotic events.

recommended_treatment.Low: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy (GDMT): SGLT2 inhibitor (Empagliflozin 10mg daily) and ACE-i/ARB; sodium restriction (<2g/day).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Quadruple GDMT: ARNI (Sacubitril/Valsartan), Beta-Blocker (Carvedilol), MRA (Spironolactone 25mg), and SGLT2i; oral Loop Diuretic (Furosemide).
recommended_treatment.High: Hospital admission for IV Loop Diuretics, inotropic support (Dobutamine/Milrinone), telemetry, and consideration of advanced mechanical therapies.

heart failure.medication_category: ARNIs, SGLT2 Inhibitors, Beta-Blockers, Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Loop Diuretics
heart failure.lifestyle_recommendations: Daily weight tracking (report > 3 lb gain in 24h), fluid restriction (1.5-2.0 L/day in severe HF), sodium restriction.
heart failure.contraindications: Non-dihydropyridine CCBs (Diltiazem, Verapamil) and NSAIDs are contraindicated in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
heart failure.red_flags: Rapid weight gain (> 5 lbs in a week), acute worsening of dyspnea at rest, orthopnea requiring > 3 pillows, pink frothy sputum.
heart failure.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute decompensated heart failure with flash pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock, severe hypoxemia.
heart failure.follow_up: Heart failure clinic follow-up within 7 to 14 days of discharge or therapy adjustment.
heart failure.evidence_source: Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA) / ACC / AHA
heart failure.rationale: Four pillars of GDMT reduce all-cause mortality and hospitalizations in HFrEF. Diuretics provide essential symptom decongestion.

recommended_treatment.Low: Short-acting bronchodilator as needed (SABA: Albuterol or SAMA: Ipratropium); smoking cessation counseling and pneumococcal vaccination.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA: Tiotropium) plus long-acting beta-agonist (LABA: Salmeterol); pulmonary rehabilitation.
recommended_treatment.High: Triple therapy (ICS + LAMA + LABA); short course oral Prednisone (40mg x 5 days) and Azithromycin if acute purulent exacerbation.

copd.medication_category: LAMAs, LABAs, Inhaled Corticosteroids, SABAs, SAMAs
copd.lifestyle_recommendations: Absolute smoking cessation, pulmonary rehabilitation exercise, avoid biomass smoke and air pollution exposure.
copd.contraindications: Do not give high-flow unmonitored oxygen in severe COPD due to risk of hypercapnic respiratory drive suppression.
copd.red_flags: Significant increase in sputum volume and purulence, acute breathlessness at rest, acute confusion, peripheral cyanosis.
copd.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute COPD exacerbation with severe acidosis (pH < 7.35), severe hypoxemia, or altered consciousness.
copd.follow_up: Pulmonary clinic visit in 4 weeks for spirometry and inhaler device verification.
copd.evidence_source: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)
copd.rationale: Dual bronchodilation with LAMA/LABA improves lung emptying and reduces exacerbation frequency. Exacerbations require corticosteroids and antibiotics.

recommended_treatment.Low: Controlled oxygen therapy via nasal cannula (target SpO2 92-96% in non-hypercapnic patients, 88-92% in COPD); treat underlying trigger.
recommended_treatment.Medium: High-Flow Nasal Cannula (HFNC) or Non-Invasive Ventilation (BiPAP/CPAP); arterial blood gas monitoring in Step-Down/ICU.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation with lung-protective tidal volumes (6 mL/kg PBW); ICU admission.

respiratory_failure.medication_category: Supplemental Oxygen, Bronchodilators, Systemic Corticosteroids, Diuretics (if cardiogenic)
respiratory_failure.lifestyle_recommendations: Strict avoidance of respiratory depressants (sedatives, opioids, alcohol).
respiratory_failure.contraindications: Avoid non-invasive ventilation if patient has facial trauma, severe emesis, high aspiration risk, or hemodynamic instability.
respiratory_failure.red_flags: Accessory muscle use, paradoxical abdominal breathing, refractory hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 < 200), acute hypercapnic encephalopathy.
respiratory_failure.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute Type I (hypoxemic) or Type II (hypercapnic) respiratory failure requiring immediate airway support.
respiratory_failure.follow_up: Daily ICU multidisciplinary rounding and post-extubation pulmonary follow-up.
respiratory_failure.guideline_version: ATS/ERS Acute Respiratory Failure Clinical Practice Guidelines 2024
respiratory_failure.evidence_source: American Thoracic Society (ATS) / European Respiratory Society (ERS)
respiratory_failure.rationale: Early non-invasive ventilation prevents intubation in hypercapnic respiratory failure. Invasive mechanical ventilation is indicated for exhaustion.

recommended_treatment.Low: Observation and optimization of medical management for underlying cause (diuretics for HF, antibiotics for parapneumonic).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Diagnostic thoracentesis (Light's criteria analysis: protein, LDH, cytology, Gram stain); therapeutic drainage if symptomatic.
recommended_treatment.High: Urgent chest tube (tube thoracostomy) insertion for complicated parapneumonic effusion or empyema; VATS evaluation.

pleural_effusion.lifestyle_recommendations: Rest during acute dyspnea, deep breathing exercises, smoking cessation.
pleural_effusion.contraindications: Avoid large-volume thoracentesis (> 1.5 L in a single procedure) to prevent re-expansion pulmonary edema.
pleural_effusion.red_flags: Loculated effusion, frank pus on aspiration (empyema), severe pleuritic chest pain with high fever and respiratory distress.
pleural_effusion.emergency_referral_conditions: Tension hydrothorax, empyema with sepsis, massive pleural effusion causing mediastinal shift.
pleural_effusion.follow_up: Repeat chest radiography within 2 to 4 weeks to ensure resolution and rule out underlying parenchymal malignancy.
pleural_effusion.rationale: Light's criteria distinguish transudates from exudates. Empyema and complicated effusions require immediate drainage to prevent fibrothorax.

recommended_treatment.Low: PESI-score low risk: Direct Oral Anticoagulant (Apixaban 10mg BID x 7 days then 5mg BID, or Rivaroxaban 15mg BID x 21 days then 20mg daily).
recommended_treatment.Medium: Submassive PE with RV strain: Inpatient therapeutic anticoagulation with LMWH (Enoxaparin 1mg/kg Q12H) or DOAC; continuous monitoring.
recommended_treatment.High: Massive PE with shock: Systemic thrombolysis (Alteplase 100mg IV over 2h) or catheter-directed embolectomy; ICU admission.

pulmonary_embolism.medication_category: Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs), LMWH, Unfractionated Heparin, Systemic Thrombolytics
pulmonary_embolism.lifestyle_recommendations: Early ambulation, wear graduated compression stockings during long travel, avoid prolonged immobility.
pulmonary_embolism.contraindications: Systemic thrombolysis is contraindicated in active internal bleeding, recent intracranial hemorrhage, or major surgery within 3 weeks.
pulmonary_embolism.red_flags: Hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg), syncope, acute RV dysfunction on echo, elevated troponin/BNP in the setting of acute dyspnea.
pulmonary_embolism.emergency_referral_conditions: Hemodynamically unstable PE (massive PE), cardiac arrest, severe refractory hypoxemia.
pulmonary_embolism.follow_up: Hematology/pulmonology clinic review at 3 months to assess duration of anticoagulation and chronic thromboembolic disease.
pulmonary_embolism.guideline_version: ESC/ERS Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism 2024
pulmonary_embolism.rationale: Anticoagulation prevents thrombus propagation and recurrent embolization. Systemic thrombolysis rapidly restores pulmonary perfusion in shock.

recommended_treatment.Low: Transient/minor stroke (NIHSS <= 3): Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (Aspirin 81mg + Clopidogrel 75mg daily for 21 days), high-intensity Statin.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Non-thrombolytic stroke: Aspirin monotherapy, telemetry monitoring, permissive hypertension (<220/120 mmHg), dysphagia screening.
recommended_treatment.High: Within 4.5h of onset: IV Thrombolysis (Tenecteplase 0.25mg/kg or Alteplase 0.9mg/kg); within 24h for LVO: Mechanical Thrombectomy.

stroke_ischemic.lifestyle_recommendations: Comprehensive stroke rehabilitation (PT/OT/SLP), strict blood pressure management, sodium restriction, Mediterranean diet.
stroke_ischemic.contraindications: Do not administer IV thrombolysis if head CT reveals hemorrhage, recent intracranial surgery, or INR > 1.7.
stroke_ischemic.red_flags: Sudden onset facial droop, arm weakness, slurred speech (FAST criteria), acute gaze deviation, decreased level of consciousness.
stroke_ischemic.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute stroke symptoms within 24 hours of onset (Code Stroke activation for emergency reperfusion).
stroke_ischemic.follow_up: Stroke neurology clinic visit at 30 and 90 days with modified Rankin Scale (mRS) functional assessment.
stroke_ischemic.guideline_version: AHA/ASA Early Management of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke Guidelines 2024
stroke_ischemic.evidence_source: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)
stroke_ischemic.rationale: Rapid arterial recanalization salvage ischemic penumbra. Time-to-treatment strongly determines functional independence.

recommended_treatment.Low: Small volume ICH: ICU monitoring, strict BP control (target SBP 130-140 mmHg via IV Nicardipine/Labetalol), serial non-contrast CT head.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Moderate ICH: Immediate reversal of anticoagulation (4-Factor PCC for Warfarin, Idarucizumab for Dabigatran, Andexanet for Xa inhibitors).
recommended_treatment.High: Large ICH with mass effect / midline shift / hydrocephalus: Urgent neurosurgical consultation for craniotomy, EVD, or decompressive hemicraniectomy.

intracranial_hemorrhage.medication_category: Anticoagulation Reversal Agents (4F-PCC, Andexanet Alfa), IV Antihypertensives, Hyperosmolar Therapy (Mannitol, 3% Saline)
intracranial_hemorrhage.lifestyle_recommendations: Rigorous lifetime blood pressure control (<130/80 mmHg), avoid alcohol and illicit sympathomimetic drugs (cocaine/methamphetamine).
intracranial_hemorrhage.contraindications: Antiplatelets, anticoagulants, and vasodilators (e.g. Nitroprusside) are strictly contraindicated in active hemorrhage.
intracranial_hemorrhage.red_flags: Sudden severe headache ('worst of life'), progressive lethargy, pupil asymmetry, Cushing's triad (bradycardia, hypertension, irregular breathing).
intracranial_hemorrhage.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute intracranial hemorrhage, expanding hematoma with neurological deterioration, impending brain herniation.
intracranial_hemorrhage.follow_up: Neurocritical care and neurosurgery follow-up with repeat MRI/CT head at 6 to 12 weeks.
intracranial_hemorrhage.evidence_source: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)
intracranial_hemorrhage.rationale: Rapid blood pressure reduction and anticoagulation reversal limit hematoma expansion and decrease secondary brain injury.

recommended_treatment.Low: Single unprovoked seizure with normal MRI/EEG: Observation, seizure precautions (no driving, avoid swimming alone), sleep hygiene.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Recurrent unprovoked seizures: Monotherapy with second-generation Antiseizure Medication (Levetiracetam 500-1000mg BID or Lamotrigine).
recommended_treatment.High: Status Epilepticus (> 5 min): IV Lorazepam (4mg) followed immediately by IV Levetiracetam (60mg/kg) or Fosphenytoin; ICU airway support.

epilepsy_seizures.medication_category: Antiseizure Medications (ASMs: Levetiracetam, Lamotrigine, Lacosamide), Benzodiazepines (Lorazepam, Midazolam)
epilepsy_seizures.lifestyle_recommendations: Ensure regular sleep schedule, avoid sleep deprivation, avoid alcohol excess and withdrawal, strictly adhere to medications.
epilepsy_seizures.contraindications: Avoid abrupt discontinuation of antiseizure medications due to high risk of breakthrough status epilepticus.
epilepsy_seizures.red_flags: Continuous seizure activity lasting > 5 minutes, failure to regain full consciousness between seizures, status epilepticus.
epilepsy_seizures.emergency_referral_conditions: Status epilepticus, seizure with major head trauma, prolonged hypoxia or cyanosis during seizure.
epilepsy_seizures.follow_up: Comprehensive epilepsy clinic follow-up within 4 weeks with routine electroencephalogram (EEG) and MRI brain.
epilepsy_seizures.guideline_version: AES/AAN Evidence-Based Guidelines for Status Epilepticus and Epilepsy 2024
epilepsy_seizures.evidence_source: American Epilepsy Society (AES) / American Academy of Neurology (AAN)
epilepsy_seizures.rationale: Early benzodiazepine administration stops status epilepticus within the critical 5-minute therapeutic window to prevent excitotoxic injury.

recommended_treatment.Low: Identify and reverse metabolic / infectious triggers: Treat UTI/pneumonia, correct mild hyponatremia/hyperglycemia, review polypharmacy.
recommended_treatment.Medium: Hepatic encephalopathy: Lactulose (20-30g TID titrated to 2-3 soft stools/day) plus Rifaximin (550mg BID); thiamine 500mg IV for Wernicke prophylaxis.
recommended_treatment.High: Severe metabolic encephalopathy with coma: Secure airway, IV Dextrose for hypoglycemia, Naloxone for suspected opioid tox, ICU telemetry.

altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.medication_category: Lactulose, Rifaximin, Thiamine, IV Dextrose, Electrolyte Replacements, Targeted Antibiotics
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.lifestyle_recommendations: Maintain orientation cues (daylight, clocks, calendars), ensure regular day-night sleep cycles, avoid anticholinergic sedatives.
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.contraindications: Avoid benzodiazepines, diphenhydramine, and opioid sedatives as they worsen delirium and metabolic encephalopathy.
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.red_flags: Rapidly deteriorating Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS < 8), non-reactive pupils, meningismus, severe hypoglycemia.
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute coma of unknown etiology, suspected bacterial meningitis / encephalitis, severe sepsis.
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.follow_up: Medical/neurology outpatient review within 2 to 4 weeks after stabilization of underlying metabolic disorder.
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.guideline_version: SCCM / AAN Clinical Practice Guidelines for Acute Encephalopathy 2024
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.evidence_source: Society of Critical Care Medicine (SCCM) / American Academy of Neurology (AAN)
altered_mental_status_encephalopathy.rationale: Encephalopathy is a symptom of underlying systemic dysfunction. Rapid resolution depends entirely on reversing the primary etiology.

recommended_treatment.Low: ABCD2 score < 4: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (Aspirin 81mg + Clopidogrel 75mg daily for 21 days), high-intensity Statin, vascular imaging within 24h.
recommended_treatment.Medium: ABCD2 score >= 4: Urgent admission to TIA unit; carotid duplex ultrasound, continuous cardiac telemetry, MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI).
recommended_treatment.High: Symptomatic severe carotid stenosis (70-99%): Urgent Carotid Endarterectomy (CEA) or stenting within 48-72 hours; full stroke prevention GDMT.

transient_ischemic_attack.lifestyle_recommendations: Tobacco cessation, Mediterranean diet, aerobic exercise, blood pressure control (<130/80 mmHg).
transient_ischemic_attack.contraindications: Do not treat TIA with full-dose therapeutic anticoagulation unless cardiac source of embolism (e.g. AFib) is proven.
transient_ischemic_attack.red_flags: Crescendo TIAs (multiple episodes in 24 hours), focal motor weakness, speech loss lasting > 15 minutes.
transient_ischemic_attack.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute TIA within 48 hours (90-day stroke risk is highest in the first 48 hours post-TIA).
transient_ischemic_attack.follow_up: Urgent outpatient neurovascular clinic visit within 7 days.
transient_ischemic_attack.guideline_version: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients with Stroke and TIA 2024
transient_ischemic_attack.evidence_source: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)
transient_ischemic_attack.rationale: Early DAPT and urgent revascularization for symptomatic carotid disease reduce the 90-day stroke risk by up to 80%.

recommended_treatment.Low: Diabetic/peripheral neuropathy: Strict glycemic control (HbA1c < 7.0%), daily foot inspection, topical Capsaicin or Lidocaine 5% patch.
recommended_treatment.Medium: First-line neuropathic pain pharmacotherapy: Duloxetine (30-60mg daily), Gabapentin (300-900mg TID), or Pregabalin (75-150mg BID).
recommended_treatment.High: Rapidly progressive weakness / suspected Guillain-Barre Syndrome: Urgent IVIG (0.4g/kg/day x 5 days) or Plasmapheresis; vital capacity monitoring.

neuropathy_neurodegenerative.medication_category: SNRIs (Duloxetine), Gabapentinoids (Gabapentin, Pregabalin), TCAs (Amitriptyline), Topical Analgesics
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.lifestyle_recommendations: Wear protective supportive footwear, perform daily visual foot examinations, avoid walking barefoot, avoid neurotoxic alcohol intake.
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.contraindications: Avoid long-term opioid analgesics for chronic neuropathic pain due to lack of efficacy and high risk of dependence.
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.red_flags: Ascending muscle weakness, bilateral foot drop, loss of deep tendon reflexes, autonomic instability, respiratory muscle weakness.
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.emergency_referral_conditions: Acute motor neuropathy with rapidly progressive paralysis or diaphragmatic weakness (Guillain-Barre).
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.follow_up: Neurology review with electromyography / nerve conduction studies (EMG/NCS) within 4 to 8 weeks.
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.guideline_version: AAN Practice Guideline: Neuropathic Pain and Peripheral Neuropathy 2024
neuropathy_neurodegenerative.rationale: Modulating central and peripheral pain pathways with SNRIs or gabapentinoids provides effective neuropathic relief without opioid risks.
